day.description: 紫微斗数开源排盘引擎, 基于倪海厦《天纪》体系，含完整排盘算法、四化系统、格局知识库、古籍原文数据
day.readme: 一、项目理念：紫微斗数是中国传统命理学的瑰宝，倪海厦老师在《天纪》中系统梳理了正宗的紫微斗数体系。我们希望通过技术手段让更多人接触和学习这门学问。 开源排盘算法和知识库，是因为我们相信：算法是公开的传统智慧，不应该被锁在围墙里。真正的价值在于解读的深度、用户体验的打磨、以及持续运营的积累。 二、项目信息：基于 倪海厦《天纪》 教学体系的紫微斗数排盘系统，包含完整排盘算法、四化系统、格局知识库、古籍原文数据，以及一套完整开源的紫微斗数解读数据：v4.0 解读数据集, , 67.5 万张命盘 × 13 维 = 877 万段解读，正文约 204 亿字，解压后 56.6 GB（2026-10-15 发布）。 v3.0 每张盘解读字数按 2,160 张盘抽样估算，其余数字为全量统计；两版每张盘都是 13 维。 在线体验：ouranic.cn，排盘、AI 解读、命盘历史全部开放。 本轮跟随网站 2026-10-15 发版（网站内容版本 ca268829f7a9）： 1.

day.description: Macro is a unified workspace for teams: email, chat, docs, tasks, agents, calls, and CRM, @-linked together with shared AI memory.
day.readme: Macro is the all-in-one workspace for you and your team. It unifies email + messages + docs + tasks + agents + CRM into a single fast interface with shared team-level memory. Everything in your workspace is @linked and searchable so your team (and your agents) never have to switch tools. We built Macro because we wanted a single operating system for our startup. There are many good software products, and we used them all, Slack, Linear, Notion, HubSpot, and Superhuman, but they don't work together as one system.

day.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
day.readme: My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy.

It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app (iOS, Android), web app and Electron-based desktop app. Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Google Antigravity. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them. Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents.

day.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

new.description: Static recompilation of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom to native Windows x86-64, with a Vulkan renderer. Game files not included.
new.readme: TotK Recomp is a static recompilation of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native Windows x86-64 application (docs/architecture.md). Early development. The game is playable on Windows; visual bugs and crashes are still expected. Report problems as issues, following CONTRIBUTING.md.

HakiOS runs the open-source XNU kernel (xnu-8796.121.2) with my own boot loader and my own drivers on an Android phone with a Qualcomm SoC, and boots the stock iOS 16.5 user space on top of it: launchd, backboardd, SpringBoard, the apps. The same thing runs in QEMU (virt, aarch64) on a Nothing is flashed. The loader goes into RAM through fastboot boot, the system lives in RAM for the length of a session, and a reboot brings the phone back to its own Android.

new.description: Create Apple style dimensional drawings of UI components.

new.description: Image-driven 3D scene generation system. Users provide a reference image and prompt words, and the system generates previewable, replayable, and traceable scene results according to the camera trajectory; official 3D demonstration assets allow direct viewing of color/depth animations and Gaussian…
new.readme: Guangyu Zaojing (光域造景) is an image-driven 3D scene generation system. You supply one reference image and a prompt, and the system generates scene results along a camera trajectory that you can preview, replay, and trace. The official 3D demo assets play color/depth animations and Gaussian point clouds directly in the browser. The web app ships as a Docker image and listens on port 8090 by default. A single image rarely turns into spatial content you can look around in, move through, and hand off.

new.description: A public release of the Steal My Bitcoin challenge
new.readme: This README explains stealmybitcoinpoc.py, a single-file Python reproduction of the request sequence used in my Steal My Bitcoin CTF run. It uses only Python's standard library. The script builds the requests itself, checks each leak before moving on, and records the HTTP bytes from a new run. This can probably be done easier without all the extra debug crap and as in my John Hammond video about the Steam Local Privilege Escalation I discovered, you could probably clean up this ugly PoC.

new.description: High fidelity scanner for php2shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
new.readme: A command-line tool for detecting CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in PHP applications. The scanner sends a minimal multipart control request followed by up to three crafted multipart probes. The probes use PHP array keys nested 62 levels deep and increase from 1 MiB to 20 MiB, matching the detection logic used by Assetnote's internal scanner.

threats.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys compromised
threats.headline: Flawed key generation exposed eMudhra intermediate CA keys, letting attackers impersonate sites to non-browser TLS clients
threats.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were incorrectly generated by the CA, so anyone can recover them from the certificates. Six are TLS intermediates trusted by the Chrome, Mozilla, Microsoft and Apple root programs, and two are codesigning intermediates trusted by Microsoft. An attacker with any of the keys could impersonate any website or service, and clients that ship their own CA bundle or do not enforce Certificate Transparency, such as curl, are most exposed.
actions: Update Python certifi to 2026.10.19 or later
Update curl CA bundle to 2026-10-20 or later
Update Homebrew ca-certificates to 2026-09-25_1 or later
Update Rust rustls-webpki to 0.103.16 or later
Update Rust webpki-roots / webpki-root-certs to 1.0.10 or later
Update Debian ca-certificates to 20250419~deb12u2, 20250419+deb13u1, 20260816+nmu1 or later
Update applications and libraries that ship their own CA bundle, including Electron apps.

action_quotes.quote: Users should update their browsers and operating systems to the latest versions as soon as possible.

action_quotes.action: Update applications and libraries that ship their own CA bundle, including Electron apps.
action_quotes.quote: These include applications and libraries that ship their own CA bundle, and apps built on Electron, such as Slack and Discord.

who: clients that ship their own CA bundle
command-line tools that do not enforce CT
threats.quote: An attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs could impersonate any website or service.

actions: Rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

action_quotes.action: Rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

who: Python clients using requests, urllib3 or pip
threats.quote: An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname.

threats.title: rustls-webpki accepts distrusted emSign intermediate certificates

threats.headline: TWCA reports unauthorized access to its Registration Authority server; investigation is ongoing
threats.summary: TWCA reported that its security monitoring detected indicators of unauthorized access to its Registration Authority server. threats.quote: TWCA's security monitoring systems detected indicators of unauthorized access to our Registration Authority (RA) server.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK HTTP transports lack request limits
threats.headline: MCP TypeScript SDK servers over HTTP accepted unlimited bodies and batches, enabling unauthenticated denial of service
threats.summary: MCP servers built with the TypeScript SDK and reachable over HTTP put no limit on POST body size or on the number of messages in a JSON-RPC batch. Large requests could exhaust server memory, and one long batch could block the server from serving anyone else. No credentials were needed unless the application authenticates requests before they reach the SDK.
actions: Cap request body size in a reverse proxy until the SDK is upgraded.

action_quotes.action: Cap request body size in a reverse proxy until the SDK is upgraded.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, cap request body size in a reverse proxy.

who: MCP servers built on the TypeScript SDK
servers reachable over Streamable HTTP by untrusted clients
threats.quote: Large requests could exhaust the server's memory, and one long batch could block it from serving anyone else.

threats.title: vLLM image loader reaches Ghostscript on untrusted EPS input
threats.headline: vLLM passes untrusted image bytes to Pillow, enabling Ghostscript command execution on vulnerable hosts.
threats.summary: The same path also exposes a separate Pillow denial-of-service condition that can exhaust media-loading workers.
actions: Restrict who can reach image-capable vLLM endpoints.

action_quotes.action: Restrict who can reach image-capable vLLM endpoints.
action_quotes.quote: API-key authentication and network access controls determine who can reach the request path.

who: hosts with a vulnerable Ghostscript build
threats.quote: On a host with Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, this exposes the known Ghostscript sandbox escape through vLLM's image-loading path and can execute commands with the vLLM process's privileges.

threats.title: vLLM SHM multimodal cache allows forged handles to reach pickle
threats.headline: Authenticated vLLM callers can forge SHM cache handles to run arbitrary Python in worker processes.
threats.summary: When the SHM multimodal processor cache is enabled, vLLM treats an address and monotonic_id pair as authority to read shared memory in the worker. A caller can forge this pair through public HTTP routes so the worker unpickles attacker-staged bytes. This lets an ordinary authenticated inference caller execute arbitrary Python in the worker process, even with insecure serialization disabled.
actions: Check whether your deployments enable the SHM multimodal processor cache.

action_quotes.action: Check whether your deployments enable the SHM multimodal processor cache.
action_quotes.quote: When --mm-processor-cache-type shm is enabled, vLLM's multimodal SHM cache represents a cached item with an address and monotonic_id pair and treats that pair as authority to dereference shared memory in the worker.

who: vLLM deployments using SHM multimodal caching
threats.quote: An ordinary authenticated inference caller can execute arbitrary Python in the worker process on a deployment that uses SHM multimodal caching.

threats.title: vLLM request-controlled processor code revision allows code execution
threats.headline: Untrusted vLLM multimodal requests can swap processor code revision, running arbitrary code on remote-code deployments
threats.summary: Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process.
actions: Keep trust_remote_code disabled where it is not required.
Put the tokenize endpoint behind authentication.

action_quotes.action: Keep trust_remote_code disabled where it is not required.
action_quotes.quote: The default trust_remote_code=False configuration is not affected.

action_quotes.action: Put the tokenize endpoint behind authentication.
action_quotes.quote: Protect /tokenize with the configured authentication policy as defense in depth.

who: deployments serving multimodal models with dynamic processor code
threats.quote: Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process.

threats.title: LiteLLM proxy arbitrary local file read via credentials alias
threats.headline: Low-privilege LiteLLM proxy users could read local files, exposing master and provider API keys
threats.summary: Reading environment files can disclose the master key and provider API keys, escalating to full proxy-admin control.
threats.quote: Reading files such as /proc/self/environ can disclose LITELLM_MASTER_KEY and provider API keys, so the impact can escalate to full proxy-admin control.

threats.title: LiteLLM proxy salt key reuse allows admin escalation
threats.headline: LiteLLM internal users could forge admin tokens and run arbitrary commands on the proxy host
threats.summary: An internal user could request an API key with a forged admin credential in its metadata, then present the encrypted result as a bearer token to gain full administrative access. That access includes executing arbitrary commands through the MCP stdio endpoint.
actions: Turn off experimental UI login until patched, accepting that CLI SSO and gateway login break.

action_quotes.action: Turn off experimental UI login until patched, accepting that CLI SSO and gateway login break.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade immediately, set EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=false .

threats.quote: An internal user can escalate to proxy admin and execute arbitrary commands on the host.

threats.title: vLLM Phi-4 multimodal audio encoder memory exhaustion
threats.headline: One legal 10-minute audio clip can crash vLLM engines serving Phi-4-multimodal-instruct
threats.summary: A single 600 second audio clip, within default limits, drove GPU memory up until the engine crashed and the server went down. An unauthenticated client that can reach the chat/completions API could take the service offline until restart.
who: models reusing the Phi-4 audio tower
threats.quote: Full denial of service, requiring a process restart.

threats.title: vLLM DeepSeek-OCR image validation crashes the engine
threats.headline: A single ordinary PNG can permanently crash vLLM servers running DeepSeek-OCR family models
threats.summary: This trips an assertion in the engine worker that is not contained per request, and the whole process tree shuts down. An unauthenticated chat request under default configuration can take the server down until a manual restart.
threats.quote: /health refuses connections until a manual restart.

threats.title: vLLM out-of-vocabulary token id crashes engine
threats.headline: A single pre-tokenized request with an out-of-range token id can crash vLLM engines serving Llama-2 models.
threats.summary: vLLM's input validation accepts a token id equal to the vocabulary size for models whose vocabulary is an exact multiple of 64, such as the Llama-2 family. At tensor-parallel size 1 the id reaches the embedding lookup out of range and raises a CUDA device-side assert that takes the engine down. Any client that can send pre-tokenized input can trigger it.
threats.quote: At tensor-parallel size 1 the embedding lookup does not mask indices, so the id reaches F.embedding out of range and raises a CUDA device-side assert, which poisons the engine's CUDA context and takes the engine down.

threats.title: vLLM chat template rendering lets one request wedge endpoints
threats.headline: Unbounded Jinja2 chat template rendering in vLLM lets one request or model repo block all chat endpoints.
threats.summary: One short authenticated request can permanently block all chat-style endpoints for every tenant until restart, and a variant can exhaust memory and kill the API server. A malicious model repo carrying a hostile template in its tokenizer config has the same effect on every replica that loads it.
threats.quote: In a multi-tenant deployment this is a cross-tenant denial-of-service from any one tenant.

threats.title: MCP Python SDK accepts bearer tokens for other services
threats.headline: MCP Python SDK servers accepted tokens issued for other services sharing the same authorization server
threats.summary: The MCP Python SDK's server-side bearer authentication had no way to check a token's audience. Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by the MCP server. Patched versions add an opt-in check that stays off unless configured.
actions: Turn on token resource validation after upgrading, since it is off by default.
Reject tokens whose audience does not include your server in the token verifier.

action_quotes.action: Turn on token resource validation after upgrading, since it is off by default.
action_quotes.quote: The patched versions add a validate_token_resource setting that is off unless you set it.

action_quotes.action: Reject tokens whose audience does not include your server in the token verifier.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, reject any token whose aud does not include your server inside verify_token() .

who: MCP servers using the Python SDK bearer authentication
servers sharing an authorization server with other services
threats.quote: Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by your MCP server.

threats.title: MCP Python SDK clients leak headers on cross-origin redirects
threats.headline: MCP Python SDK HTTP clients sent custom credential headers and bodies to any redirect target
threats.summary: Anyone able to make a trusted endpoint redirect elsewhere could capture that material.
actions: Rotate credentials that a client may have sent through a redirect to an untrusted host.

action_quotes.action: Rotate credentials that a client may have sent through a redirect to an untrusted host.
action_quotes.quote: If a client may already have followed a redirect to a host you do not control, rotate the credentials it carried.

who: applications using the MCP Python SDK as an HTTP client
threats.quote: Anyone able to make an endpoint you trust redirect elsewhere (a stale redirect to a lapsed domain, a misrouted proxy rule, redirect logic an attacker can influence) could capture that material.

threats.title: MCP Python SDK client fetches server-chosen schema references
threats.headline: Malicious MCP servers could make Python SDK clients fetch URLs, read local files, or freeze
threats.summary: A server could make the client request a URL or read a local file from the client's own network position on every tool call. A target that held the connection open could freeze every session in the client process.
actions: Call tools only on trusted servers until upgraded.

action_quotes.action: Call tools only on trusted servers until upgraded.
action_quotes.quote: Until you can upgrade, call tools only on servers you trust.

who: applications using the MCP Python SDK as a client
clients calling tools on servers they do not control
threats.quote: the fetch ran synchronously on the event loop with no timeout, so a target that accepted the connection and then went quiet froze every session in the process for as long as it held the connection.

threats.title: LiteLLM proxy reflected XSS in SSO debug callback
threats.headline: Unauthenticated LiteLLM SSO debug route allowed script injection leading to proxy admin account takeover
threats.summary: An attacker with an account on the configured identity provider could craft a callback URL and deliver it to a logged-in proxy admin. Scripts running in the proxy origin can read the dashboard session cookie and act with the victim's privileges.
threats.quote: Scripts executing in the proxy origin can read the dashboard session cookie and act with the victim's privileges, up to full admin account takeover.

items.title: Platform teams can gate every agent skill install behind a scan this quarter
items.connection: The Cursor Marketplace backdoor shows agent add-ons are a live supply chain risk, npx skills gives one install path to control, and SkillSpector can scan skills for injection and exfiltration before that path lets them through.
items.context: most engineering orgs already route package installs through an approved registry
chain: A backdoored Claude Code for VS Code listing gives security teams a concrete incident to point to.
Skills carry the same broad access as extensions, and npx skills turns installing them into one command line step that can be wrapped.
Wrapping that step with a SkillSpector scan creates an internal allowlisted skills registry, the same pattern firms already use for npm.
Once a registry exists, popular public skill sets such as copied .agents directories can be admitted after review instead of banned outright.
items.who: Platform and AppSec teams at software companies benefit; the CISO budget pays, or a consultancy sells it as a fixed-fee setup.
items.variable: share of agent skills installed without review
items.versus: Doing nothing leaves developers copying skills with machine access, and banning skills outright just pushes the copying out of sight.
items.smallest_test: Wrap npx skills in a script that runs SkillSpector first, feed it a set of public skills plus a few seeded with known exfiltration patterns, and count success if every seeded skill is blocked and fewer than one in ten clean skills is falsely flagged.
items.disconfirm: SkillSpector misses the seeded exfiltration skills or flags so many clean ones that developers bypass the wrapper.

items.body: Agents such as Claude Agent and Codex can reach the emulator, build system, Logcat and Compose Previews, so a team can standardize on one agent across tools. That broad access is also why vetting each agent's source matters. There is no evidence yet on agent quality inside the IDE.

items.lead: Inference is getting cheaper from both ends, on shared servers and on local hardware.
items.body: SGLang's peak throughput on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash rose from 654K to 1.09 million tokens per second per GPU in four days, though that is a vendor-run figure on one setup. Locally, you can test whether the Clover diffusion mixture-of-experts matches an autoregressive Qwen model, and transcribe English on any CPU at a 5.21% average word error rate. Both rest on thin evidence: one reviewer's test of a preview, and a model-card claim.
